name: BEST
summary: BEST tested the gallium source anomaly using an intense chromium-51 electron-neutrino source and two concentric liquid-gallium targets at Baksan. It compared capture rates at metre-scale distances, providing a source-based complement to reactor disappearance experiments.
detection_principle: Electron neutrinos convert gallium-71 into germanium-71. Germanium atoms are chemically extracted after each exposure and their electron-capture decays counted in low-background proportional counters; the inner and outer zones probe different path lengths.

status.label: Completed / historical
status.evidence: The cited publication documents this stage; its publication date is distinct from the data-taking period.

key_parameters.name: Gallium target
key_parameters.value: Approximately 47 tonnes, divided into two zones

results.summary: Both zones showed deficits relative to calculated production rates. Their similar suppression confirms the gallium anomaly but does not by itself identify a sterile neutrino or resolve cross-section and other explanations.

science_scope: An artificial-source radiochemical experiment, rather than a separate solar-neutrino observatory.
